correctness.rationale: The fair-cut representation gives n=N−1 and (K,M)=(1+S,1+R). For k zero-run starts, compressing out the kr prescribed zeros gives the two binomial counts, with p^k or p^(k−1) according as the first start is interior or at the boundary. The Bernoulli score identity gives −(1/4)∑F′. At r=m+j the binomial terms divided by k! are dominated by an exponential series, including their scaled derivatives, and the limit of F′/m is 2x_j exp(−x_j). For the derivative tails the union of candidate windows about a pivotal site has length at most 2r−1; when r≤n/8 a disjoint length-≥n/4 segment gives an independent no-run condition, bounded using independent geometric runs and a binomial lower-tail bound. This yields summable centered tails; the omitted r>n/8 terms are exponentially small. The analogous probability tails give uniform integrability, so the phase-specific variance and the covariance normalization by sqrt(n)/2 are valid. Mellin integration over adjacent dyadic intervals gives the stated Gamma coefficients. Independent integer enumeration via aggregate cut counts (python3 /workspace/audit_evidence/composition_count_check.py) recovered −7/8 for four bits and the three finite table comparisons within 2.4e−7. Those checks are diagnostic; the all-sequence claim follows from the tail estimates.
